items.title: Booking Request Model & Migration
items.description: Add a BookingRequest model to Prisma schema. This represents a user's request to be matched for a specific time slot and duration. A booking request is PENDING until matched, then MATCHED (linked to a Session), or EXPIRED if no partner was found before the session start cutoff.
steps: BookingRequest model added to schema.prisma

Fields: id (cuid), userId, slotTime (DateTime), durationMin (Int: 25|50|75), status (BookingRequestStatus enum: PENDING, MATCHED, CANCELLED, EXPIRED), sessionId (optional — set when matched), createdAt, updatedAt
BookingRequestStatus enum created
Relation: BookingRequest → User (many-to-one)
Relation: BookingRequest → Session (optional many-to-one)
Index on: bookingRequests.slotTime, bookingRequests.status, bookingRequests.userId
Unique constraint: @@unique([userId, slotTime, durationMin]) — one booking per user per slot+duration
Add bookingRequests relation to User model
Add bookingRequests relation to Session model
Migration created and applied successfully: prisma migrate dev --name add-booking-request
prisma generate succeeds
npm run typecheck passes

items.title: Matching Service — Core Algorithm with Race Condition Protection
items.description: Implement the matching service that pairs users. When a booking request is created, atomically find the earliest unmatched booking in the same slot and duration (excluding blocked users), create a session, and mark both bookings as matched. Use Prisma interactive transactions to prevent double-matching race conditions.
steps: MatchingService class created at apps/api/src/matching/matching.service.ts
Method: matchBookingRequest(bookingRequestId: string) → Promise<Session | null>
Uses Prisma interactive transaction: prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => { ... }, { isolationLevel: Prisma.TransactionIsolationLevel.Serializable })
Within transaction: fetch the requesting BookingRequest by ID (verify it is PENDING)
Within transaction: find earliest PENDING BookingRequest where slotTime matches, durationMin matches, userId != requesting user, ordered by createdAt ASC
Excludes users who have a Block relationship with the requesting user — query: find all blockedIds where blockerId = requestingUserId OR blockedId = requestingUserId, exclude those userIds
Excludes users where isBanned = true OR isActive = false

If match found: create Session record — user1Id = matched booking userId (earlier), user2Id = requesting booking userId, status = CONFIRMED, scheduledAt = slotTime, durationMin = durationMin, livekitRoomName = generated session id
Update both BookingRequests: status = MATCHED, sessionId = new session id
Return the created Session with user relations included
If no match found: return null, requesting booking stays PENDING
All DB operations inside the single transaction — atomic commit or full rollback
Unit test: two users booking same slot and duration get matched
Unit test: third user booking same slot stays PENDING (only pairs of 2)
Unit test: blocked users are not matched together (test both block directions)
Unit test: banned users excluded from matching
Unit test: inactive users excluded from matching
Unit test: concurrent matching attempts don't double-match — run 5 parallel matchBookingRequest calls for 3 bookings, verify exactly 1 pair matched and 1 stays PENDING
Unit test: requesting a non-PENDING booking returns null gracefully
npm run test passes
items.notes: This is the most critical piece of the matching engine. Race conditions here mean double-booking. Use Prisma $transaction with Serializable isolation. Test the concurrent case thoroughly — this is the whole point of using transactions.

items.title: Booking Request API — Cancel
items.description: Implement DELETE /api/bookings/:id to cancel a pending booking request. If the booking was already matched, handle graceful unmatching — cancel the session, return the partner's booking to PENDING, and re-trigger matching for the partner.
steps: DELETE /api/bookings/:id endpoint exists
Fetch booking by ID — return 404 if not found
Authorization: only the booking owner (userId == req.user.id) can cancel — return 403 otherwise
If booking status is EXPIRED or CANCELLED: return 400 'Booking is already cancelled or expired'
If booking status is PENDING: set status=CANCELLED. Remove scheduled expiry BullMQ job. Done.

If booking status is MATCHED: begin transaction — set booking status=CANCELLED, set linked session status=CANCELLED, find partner's BookingRequest for this session and set it back to status=PENDING with sessionId=null
After transaction: remove scheduled no-show job, remove scheduled reminder jobs for the cancelled session
After transaction: call MatchingService.matchBookingRequest(partnerBookingId) to re-trigger matching for the partner
Late cancellation penalty: if slotTime is within 1 hour from now AND booking was MATCHED, increment user's strikeCount by 1
If strikeCount reaches 3 after increment: send warning email via Resend
If strikeCount reaches 5 after increment: set isBanned=true, send ban email
Response: { success: true, message: 'Booking cancelled' }

Unit test: cancel MATCHED booking — session CANCELLED, partner booking back to PENDING
Unit test: partner re-matching triggered after cancel
Unit test: late cancellation (within 1 hour) adds strike
Unit test: early cancellation (>1 hour away) does NOT add strike

items.title: No-Show Detection — BullMQ Scheduled Job
items.description: Schedule a BullMQ job at session start time + 5 minutes. If the session is still CONFIRMED (not ACTIVE — meaning at least one user hasn't joined), mark it as NO_SHOW. Increment strikeCount for the absent user. Notify the present user.
steps: In MatchingService or SessionService: when session status set to CONFIRMED, call scheduleNoshowCheck(sessionId, scheduledAt)
scheduleNoshowCheck: creates delayed job in 'session-noshow' queue, delay = (scheduledAt + 5 minutes) - now, jobId = noshow-{sessionId}
noshow.worker.ts processes the job:
1. Fetch session by sessionId from job data
2. If session.status !== 'CONFIRMED' (already ACTIVE, COMPLETED, or CANCELLED): log 'Session already progressed, skipping' and return
3. If session.status === 'CONFIRMED': at least one user didn't join within 5 min
4. Determine who joined: check Redis or DB for join tracking (from Phase 1 P1-20 implementation). Users who called PATCH /api/sessions/:id/join are 'present'. Users who didn't are 'absent'.
5. Set session.status = NO_SHOW
6. For each absent user: increment user.strikeCount by 1 via prisma.user.update
7. If user.strikeCount reaches 3: send warning email — 'Your account has received 3 strikes for no-shows. Further violations may result in suspension.'
8. If user.strikeCount reaches 5: set user.isBanned = true, send ban email — 'Your account has been suspended due to repeated no-shows.'
9. For each present user (if any): send 'partner no-show' notification via WebSocket + email
10. WebSocket event: 'session:noshow' with payload { sessionId, message: 'Your partner did not join the session.' }
Remove reminder jobs for this session (they're no longer relevant)
CRITICAL: NO_SHOW is triggered ONLY by this BullMQ job at T+5min. NEVER trigger no-show on LiveKit disconnect.
Unit test: session stays CONFIRMED after 5 min → marked NO_SHOW
Unit test: session already ACTIVE → job is no-op
Unit test: session already CANCELLED → job is no-op
Unit test: absent user's strikeCount incremented

Unit test: user banned at strikeCount=5
Unit test: present user notified of partner no-show
Unit test: both users absent → both get strikes

items.notes: HARD CONSTRAINT: No-show triggers at T+5min via BullMQ scheduled job, NOT on disconnect event. This is non-negotiable per the architecture spec.

items.title: Session Reminder — BullMQ Scheduled Jobs
items.description: Schedule reminder notifications when a session is confirmed. 24-hour reminder (email + in-app) and 5-minute reminder (in-app only).
steps: In MatchingService or SessionService: when session CONFIRMED, call scheduleReminders(sessionId, scheduledAt)
scheduleReminders creates TWO delayed jobs in 'session-reminder' queue:

Job 1: delay = (scheduledAt - 24 hours) - now. jobId = reminder-24h-{sessionId}. data = { sessionId, type: '24h' }. Only scheduled if scheduledAt is more than 24h away. If less than 24h, skip this job.
Job 2: delay = (scheduledAt - 5 minutes) - now. jobId = reminder-5m-{sessionId}. data = { sessionId, type: '5min' }. Only scheduled if scheduledAt is more than 5min away.
reminder.worker.ts processes jobs:
1. Fetch session by sessionId
2. If session.status is CANCELLED, COMPLETED, or NO_SHOW: log and skip (no-op)
3. If type === '24h': send email to both users (Resend) + WebSocket 'session:reminder' event
4. Email template: 'Reminder: Your focus session with {partnerName} is tomorrow at {time}'
5. If type === '5min': send WebSocket 'session:reminder-urgent' event ONLY (no email)
6. WebSocket payload: { sessionId, type, scheduledAt, partnerName, joinUrl: '/session/{sessionId}' }
Frontend: in useMatchNotifications or new useSessionReminders hook, listen for 'session:reminder' and 'session:reminder-urgent'
On 'session:reminder': show toast — 'Reminder: Your session with {partnerName} is tomorrow at {time}'
On 'session:reminder-urgent': show prominent toast — 'Your session starts in 5 minutes!' with 'Join Now' button linking to /session/{sessionId}
When session is CANCELLED: remove both reminder jobs via removeJob('session-reminder', 'reminder-24h-{sessionId}') and removeJob('session-reminder', 'reminder-5m-{sessionId}')
Unit test: reminder jobs scheduled on session confirmation
Unit test: 24h job not scheduled if session is <24h away
Unit test: cancelled session → reminder job is no-op
Unit test: ACTIVE session at reminder time → still sends (session started but reminder is fine)
npm run test passes

items.title: Booking Expiry — Unmatched Cleanup
items.description: Schedule a BullMQ job for each PENDING booking that fires at the slot time. If the booking is still PENDING when the slot arrives, mark it as EXPIRED and notify the user.
steps: In POST /api/bookings: when no immediate match found, call scheduleBookingExpiry(bookingRequestId, slotTime)
scheduleBookingExpiry: creates delayed job in 'booking-expiry' queue, delay = slotTime - now, jobId = expiry-{bookingRequestId}
expiry.worker.ts processes job:
1. Fetch BookingRequest by id from job data
2. If status !== 'PENDING': log and skip (already matched, cancelled, or expired)
3. Set status = EXPIRED
4. Send WebSocket notification: 'booking:expired' with { bookingRequestId, slotTime, message: 'No partner was found for your session.' }
5. Send email: 'Unfortunately, no partner was available for your {time} focus session. Book another?'
6. Email includes CTA button linking to /dashboard/book
When booking becomes MATCHED: remove expiry job via removeJob('booking-expiry', 'expiry-{bookingRequestId}')
When booking is CANCELLED: remove expiry job
Frontend: listen for 'booking:expired' event, show toast: 'No partner found for your {time} session'
Frontend: invalidate bookings query to remove expired card from dashboard
Unit test: PENDING booking expires at slot time
Unit test: already MATCHED booking → expiry job is no-op
Unit test: already CANCELLED booking → expiry job is no-op
npm run test passes

items.title: Reconnection Handling — LiveKit Disconnect Recovery
items.description: Handle LiveKit disconnections gracefully during active sessions. Session state is server-authoritative — client recovers from DB.
steps: LiveKit <LiveKitRoom> onDisconnected callback does NOT call /api/sessions/:id/complete
On disconnect: show full-screen overlay 'Reconnecting...' with spinner animation
LiveKit SDK handles automatic reconnect attempt (built-in behavior with adaptiveStream: true)
If reconnected (onConnected fires again): dismiss overlay, session continues normally
If reconnect fails after SDK attempts: show 'Connection Lost' overlay with 'Try Again' button and 'Leave Session' button
'Try Again': fetch new token from GET /api/sessions/:id/token, re-initialize LiveKit connection
'Leave Session': navigate to /dashboard
Partner sees status indicator: 'Partner reconnecting...' message near partner video tile
Session timer continues running during disconnect (calculated from server startedAt, not paused)
On page refresh during ACTIVE session: page fetches session details, gets new token, rejoins LiveKit room. Timer continues from correct position.
Only explicit actions end a session: timer reaching 0 triggers /api/sessions/:id/complete, or user clicking 'Leave Session'
Do NOT mark session as NO_SHOW on disconnect. NO_SHOW is ONLY for users who never joined (handled by BullMQ job in P2-10)
Frontend: session/[id] page checks session.status on mount — if ACTIVE and startedAt exists, calculate remaining time and resume timer
